title: Hampton vs MorganState: control, tuition, size
summary: Hampton University (Hampton) versus Morgan State University (MorganState). Also searched as MorganState vs Hampton. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Morgan State University and Hampton University differ significantly in several key aspects. Morgan State University is a public institution located in Baltimore, with an undergraduate enrollment of 9,019 students. In contrast, Hampton University is a private nonprofit university situated in Hampton, enrolling 3,727 undergraduates. Tuition costs also vary notably between the two, with Morgan State charging $8,229 for in-state students, while Hampton's in-state tuition is substantially higher at $30,592. These differences highlight the distinct profiles of Morgan State University versus Hampton University, reflecting variations in ownership, size, location, and cost.

When comparing Morgan State versus Hampton, the public versus private status is a primary distinction. Morgan State's larger undergraduate population and lower in-state tuition contrast with Hampton's smaller enrollment and higher tuition fees. The cities of Baltimore and Hampton further differentiate the institutions, contributing to their unique campus environments and regional influences.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Cost is a significant factor when comparing Morgan State University versus Hampton University. Morgan State, as a public university, charges $8,229 for in-state tuition, whereas Hampton University, a private institution, has an in-state tuition of $30,592. For out-of-state students, Morgan State's tuition is $19,124, while Hampton's out-of-state tuition remains $30,592. These figures illustrate the substantial difference in tuition fees between the two schools.

Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at Morgan State University is $27,250, slightly higher than Hampton University's median debt of $25,442. This comparison of Morgan State versus Hampton highlights the financial considerations prospective students must evaluate, including tuition costs and potential debt upon graduation.

sections.heading: Pick MorganState if
paragraphs: Pick Morgan State if you prefer a public university with a higher admission rate, as Morgan State University has an admission rate of approximately 82.23%. This makes it more accessible compared to many private institutions. Additionally, Morgan State offers a more affordable in-state tuition of $8,229, which can be a significant consideration for Maryland residents. The university's completion rate within 150% of the expected time is about 40.87%, reflecting the proportion of students who finish their programs in a timely manner. These factors make Morgan State University a suitable choice for students seeking a public education with relatively lower tuition costs and a more open admissions policy when comparing Morgan State University versus Hampton University.

sections.heading: Pick Hampton if
paragraphs: Pick Hampton if you prefer a private nonprofit institution, as Hampton University is classified under ownership code 2 by College Scorecard. The university has an admission rate of approximately 62.25%, indicating a moderately selective admissions process compared to Morgan State University. Tuition at Hampton is significantly higher, with in-state costs at $30,592, reflecting its private status. Additionally, Hampton boasts a completion rate within 150% of the expected time of about 57.16%, which is higher than that of Morgan State. These factors make Hampton University a suitable choice for students seeking a private education with a relatively higher completion rate when considering MorganState versus Hampton.
